reasonCode.text: Dysuria with flank pain and fever

note.text: HPI: 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes reporting one day of dysuria now accompanied by right-sided flank and lower-back pain, fever (38.9 C), and nausea. The combination of lower urinary tract symptoms with flank pain and systemic features raises concern for pyelonephritis, and her diabetes lowers the threshold for same-day assessment.
Action: Attend an urgent care clinic or same-day GP appointment today for examination, urine testing, and likely antibiotics.
Action: Keep up fluid intake and continue paracetamol for fever in the meantime.
Action: Go to the emergency department if you develop rigors with shaking, confusion, persistent vomiting, or are unable to keep fluids down.
Red flag: fever with flank pain (possible pyelonephritis)
Red flag: fever in a patient with diabetes

Guideline: 0.88|UTI Triage (uc-uti-001)|Burning on urination, frequency, and lower abdominal discomfort can suggest urinary tract infection. With high fever, flank pain, or vomiting, pyelonephritis is possible and warrants urgent care.

Guideline: 0.80|Adult Fever Triage (uc-fever-001)|Adult fever above 39.4 C, or fever with confusion, stiff neck, rash, or shortness of breath, requires urgent or emergency evaluation. Fever in patients with diabetes or who are immunocompromised should be seen the same day.

Action: Attend an urgent care clinic or emergency department today for examination and assessment for appendicitis.
